summary: Location.childLocations gained unintended orphanRemoval=true in the JPA migration
description:
Background
The 2.6.x Location.hbm.xml mapped childLocations with cascade="all" — removing a child from the in-memory collection did not delete the row. The migrated annotation in Location.java adds orphanRemoval = true, so any code that removes an entry from childLocations (e.g. re-parenting a location) now silently issues a DELETE of that location row on flush. This is a behavior change with both a data-loss risk and unplanned write/lock cost, and it was not part of any intentional feature.
Requested change
Remove orphanRemoval = true from Location.childLocations to restore the 2.6.x cascade semantics.
Acceptance criteria
Removing a location from a parent's childLocations collection and saving no longer deletes the child row; re-parenting works as it did in 2.6.x.

A unit test covers the re-parenting scenario to prevent the delete behavior from returning.
